title: An 0.8B assistant calls tools on the device. It is not for a high-stakes job.
friendlyTitle: A small model can use tools on your own device. It is not for important decisions.
summary: On 11 November, Tether's QVAC group released BotPsy, a 0.8 billion-parameter model built on Qwen3.5-0.8B for tool use on a device. The authors say it is for low- and medium-difficulty tasks such as search, calendar, files, and simple commerce, and that it is not for high-stakes use. On their tests it leads models up to 1.2 billion parameters on six tool benchmarks, and beats a 2 billion-parameter Qwen on five of the six. Weights and GGUF files are on Hugging Face.
friendlySummary: On 11 November, a Tether research group released BotPsy. It has 0.8 billion parameters and is built to call tools on a device, not in the cloud. The authors say it fits simple jobs, such as search, calendar, files, and basic shopping help. They say it is not for high-stakes use. On their tests it beat other small models, including a model more than twice its size on five of six tool tests. The files are on Hugging Face.
whyItMatters: A routine tool call does not need a frontier bill, and it does not need to leave the machine. The useful limit is in the same post. On the authors' red-team, BotPsy still produced an unsafe response 21 percent of the time, down from 36 percent for its base model. Under prompt injection, that rate was 31 percent. A smaller local model can draft the next step. It should not be the only check on a payment, a medical note, or a message you cannot take back.
friendlyWhyItMatters: A simple tool call does not need an expensive cloud model, and it does not have to leave your computer. The same post gives the limit.
